items.title: David Spinozza interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, NY, September 27, 2025
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] And you played with Thad Jones-Mel Lewis. [INTERVIEWEE] I did play with Thad Jones.

ctx.x: He usually played. He’s quite a good acoustic guitar player, Paul Simon. Yeah. He’s a good acoustic guitar player. So he’d play and he’d show you the song. So that’s what I’m saying, you go from that let’s say, to Thad Jones-Mel Lewis, now it’s all written out. Two completely different ways of recording you know. And sometimes, like I said, sometimes you’d walk in, you’d work on a song for two days. I’ve done sessions where you did an © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-

album in two days. You did eight, ten tracks in two days. But some of the rock stuff, the pop stuff, they were more interested in the sonic thing on it too so they’d work on drum sounds for hours. They’d work on a synth sound for hours. It was more about let’s call it the soundscaping of the record. How it sounded. Moreso than just the notes you know what I mean. So it’s a whole different – you have to be prepared. Are we going to play seventeen songs in three hours or one song for three days. Very different.

items.title: David Spinozza interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, NY, September 27, 2025
items.q: I did play with Thad Jones. ... I wound up playing on that album.

ctx.x: And you played with Thad Jones-Mel Lewis.
I did play with Thad Jones.
I have to hear this story again.
